CV · Email · Google Scholar

I am a final-year PhD candidate in Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University, advised by Professor Tze Meng Low.

My vision is for efficient code to be accessible for every workload and computing device. I believe that the way to this future is by making performance engineering systematic, reusable, and accessible.

Systematic: I discover new ways to write efficient code as the landscape of what we compute and where changes. My work has explored this question across graph algorithms, radar digital signal processing, and machine learning systems.

Reusable: I distill efficient designs into performance patterns by identifying salient architectural features and mapping them to parameters in the patterns. SMaLL, for example, captures reusable structure for building architecture-specialized machine learning libraries.

Accessible: I ask how we can bring performance expertise to the most people. Building on the distilled systems from my prior work, I work with large language models to productively generate highly specialized code.

My research interests broadly lie at the intersection of high-performance computing, programming models, machine learning systems, and, in the future, human-computer interaction.
